title: Tangent to a parametric exponential curve at t=0

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official published MS PDF (UCLES 2020). Candidates did not sit the June 2020 series (COVID-19); the MS was published to support teaching and was not reviewed against live scripts. Official MS final answer: y = 2x + 6 (or equivalent).

stem:
A curve has parametric equations \(x=\mathrm{e}^{t}-2\mathrm{e}^{-t}\), \(y=3\mathrm{e}^{2t}+1\).
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point for which \(t=0\).

steps.name: d
steps.note: MS: B1 state dx/dt = e^t + 2e^(-t), dy/dt = 6e^(2t).

steps.name: q
steps.text_tex: \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t}\), either in terms of \(t\) or after substituting \(t=0\).
steps.note: MS: *M1 use dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) either in terms of t or after substitution of t=0.

steps.name: g
steps.note: MS: A1 obtain gradient of tangent is 2.

steps.name: eq
steps.text_tex: At \(t=0\) the point is \((-1,\,4)\). Attempt the tangent with numerical gradient and these coordinates.
steps.note: MS: DM1 attempt equation of tangent with numerical gradient and coordinates.

steps.name: ans
steps.note: MS: A1 obtain y=2x+6 or equivalent.

title: Parametric log curve: dy/dx and the normal at t=1

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official MS PDF (UCLES 2017). The expression for dy/dx is symbolic, so part (i) and the equation in part (ii) are self-marked.

stem: The parametric equations of a curve are \(x=t^2+1\), \(y=4t+\ln(2t-1)\).

steps.name: dy
steps.note: MS: B1 state dy/dt = 4 + 2/(2t−1).

steps.name: q
steps.note: MS: M1 use dy/dx = (dy/dt)÷(dx/dt).

steps.name: ans
steps.note: MS: A1 obtain dy/dx=(8t−2)/(2t(2t−1)), or equivalent e.g. 2/t + 2/(4t^2−2t).

steps.name: gn
steps.text_tex: (ii) At \(t=1\), \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\dfrac{6}{2}=3\), so the gradient of the normal is \(-\dfrac13\).
steps.note: MS: M1 use a correct method to find the gradient of the normal at t=1.

steps.name: pt
steps.text_tex: The point is \((2,\,4)\). The normal has equation \(y-4=-\dfrac13(x-2)\).
steps.note: MS: M1 use a correct method to form an equation for the normal at t=1.

steps.name: ii_ans
steps.note: MS: A1 obtain final answer x+3y−14=0, or a horizontal equivalent (an integer multiple of this equation).
